name: Alaska
about: The blueprint of Alaska (perfectnations.com/perfect-states/alaska/). Census, NAEP and USDA figures marked "computed" are read by tools/build_us_state.py from data/us/raw/alaska/ and data/us-states.json. Alaska is reported by 30 boroughs and census areas (Chugach and Copper River since 2019); the map follows the Census. No figure is estimated.
notes: v1.0: Perfect Alaska, a Perfect States blueprint (Preeti Sinha, President and CEO, 25 Nov 2026: "go ahead and implement" the Perfect States plan). Water and Energy are shown as not yet measured: no primary state figure was confirmed.

assets.title: Five assets that can carry Perfect Alaska.
assets.line: Each is owned by Alaskans today and can carry a standard of living.

items.name: The Permanent Fund
items.line: The largest sovereign wealth fund in the United States, saved from oil since 1976; its draw supplies more than 66% of the State’s general fund revenue.

items.name: The land
items.line: Uplands conveyed to the people of Alaska under the Statehood Act, with more still to come.

items.name: The coast
items.line: Coastline, with 65 million acres of tidelands, shorelands and submerged lands managed by the State.

items.name: The water
items.line: The State owns its fresh water, about 40% of the entire nation’s fresh water flow.

items.name: The people
items.line: Alaskans on 1 July 2025: the asset every other asset serves.

solutions.title: Solutions for Perfect Alaska, in order.
solutions.line: Health first: no other state’s gap is as wide against the nation.

items.challenge: computed:uninsured of Alaskans had no health insurance in 2025, against computed:uninsured_us nationally.
items.advises: Create a health dividend: a slice of the Permanent Fund draw that guarantees coverage for uninsured residents, starting in Kusilvak and the rural census areas, with clinics paid on enrolment and outcomes.

items.challenge: computed:reading of fourth graders read at the NAEP Proficient level in 2024.
items.advises: Endow early reading from the Fund’s earnings and pay schools on measured reading gains, village by village.

items.challenge: 2,655 Alaskans had no home on one night in January 2025, up 39.2% since 2019.
items.advises: Back an Alaska housing bond with State land: ground leases on surplus land near jobs repay investors as homes are built.

solutions.hold: Phase 3, hold the line: food (computed:food of households food insecure) and livelihood (computed:poverty below the poverty line), with water and energy measured next.

intelligence.title: A delayed SNAP bill, and the time to cut it.
intelligence.line: From October 2027 every state pays part of its SNAP food benefits unless at least 94 of every 100 dollars are paid exactly right. AI that checks every case before it is paid can shrink that bill.
intelligence.bill_label: a year in SNAP benefits once the delayed start ends, at the full 15% share

facts.label: of SNAP dollars paid in error, 2025
start for states at or above 13.33%; then up to 15% of benefits

intelligence.advises: Use the delay. The aim is under 6%, where the State pays nothing; falling only part of the way ends the delay and brings a 15% bill forward. Pair AI case review with village caseworkers, and audit it for underpayments as well as overpayments.
